text: Calcium carbonate, CaCO (s), decomposes when heated, as shown.
CaCO (s) CaO(s) + CO (g)
The enthalpy change of reaction, ∆H , for the thermal decomposition of CaCO (s) cannot be
r 3
measured directly. Instead, a procedure involving two experiments is used. In each experiment,
the enthalpy change of a different reaction is determined.
The equation for the reaction in experiment 1 is shown. The enthalpy change for this reaction is ∆H .
experiment 1 CaCO (s) + 2HCl (aq) CaCl (aq) + H O(l) + CO (g)
The equation for the reaction in experiment 2 is shown. The enthalpy change for this reaction is ∆H .
experiment 2 CaO(s) + 2HCl (aq) CaCl (aq) + H O(l)
Experiment 1
step 1 Weigh a 0.0500 mol sample of powdered CaCO (s).
step 2 Transfer 50.00 cm , an excess, of 2.00 mol dm hydrochloric acid, HCl(aq), into a small
glass beaker.
step 3 Start a timer and measure the temperature of the HCl(aq) in the beaker every 30 seconds
for 2 minutes.
step 4 After 3 minutes add the sample of CaCO (s) to the HCl(aq) in the beaker. Continue
measuring the temperature of the reaction mixture every 30 seconds for a further
Experiment 2
Repeat experiment 1 using calcium oxide, CaO(s), instead of CaCO (s).

text: This question is about an experiment to investigate the effect of temperature on the equilibrium
constant, K , of the reaction shown.
Fe (aq) + SCN (aq) FeSCN (aq)
The data collected is used to determine the value of the enthalpy change of the reaction.
To set up the equilibrium, aqueous iron(III) nitrate, Fe(NO ) (aq), is mixed with aqueous potassium
thiocyanate, KSCN(aq). Aqueous iron thiocyanate ions, FeSCN (aq), have a red colour.
A colorimeter is used to measure the absorbance of the reaction mixture. A calibration graph can
then be used to determine the concentration of FeSCN (aq) in the reaction mixture.
